research_rejections.title: Martin Mystery
research_rejections.reason: Although supernatural creatures and episodic mysteries recur, independent series descriptions and reviews identify a teen-focused comedic cartoon with lightweight stakes rather than sustained mature high-fantasy worldbuilding, faction conflict or serious mythic stakes. Sources: https://www.commonsensemedia.org/tv-reviews/martin-mystery and https://www.allocine.fr/series/ficheserie_gen_cserie%3D5321.html

research_rejections.title: Scooby-Doo on Zombie Island
research_rejections.reason: Real supernatural threats and a darker-than-usual mystery are present, but the film remains explicitly classified as children's/family mystery-comedy rather than a serious mature fantasy with developed magic systems, kingdoms or factions. Sources: https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/scoobydoo-on-zombie-island and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scooby-Doo_on_Zombie_Island

research_rejections.title: The Cat Creature
research_rejections.reason: A supernatural feline curse drives this short made-for-TV horror mystery, but available descriptions do not support the breadth of fantasy worldbuilding, magic systems, multiple races or epic conflict required for a strong baseline fit. The production's deliberate 1940s-style horror aesthetic is noted separately from release year. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cat_Creature
